y-m-36-03.title: If one root is 1+i, what is the other?
y-m-36-03.goal: Check judgments as info arrives to find conditions (coefficient type) guaranteeing conjugate-root property.
y-m-36-03.material: One root of x²+px+q=0 is 1+i. (i imaginary unit, i²=−1; read 'eye'.) Each new fact arrives separately; judge what can be said about other root.
y-m-36-03.thinking.0: Sort out how much known info lets you conclude
y-m-36-03.thinking.2: Find conditions for property and counterexamples
y-m-36-03.prereq.0: Complex a+bi and conjugate complex numbers, i²=−1
y-m-36-03.prereq.1: Express sum/product of quadratic roots through coefficients (grade 10 equations level). H2 here only production difficulty/support, not grade assignment. Assume prerequisites learned.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.prompt: Each step choose what can be said from information known now about other root.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.hint.0: Each time, note whether new info concerns p,q or roots.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.hint.1: Calculate sum and product yourself; check if they are real numbers.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.info: Known: one root is 1+i. Nothing says what kind of numbers p,q are.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Can the other root be fixed from this alone?
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.after: If p,q kind unknown, other root could be anything; honestly say cannot fix. If you silently assumed real p,q and answer 1−i, next step checks whether that assumption was given.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Problem doesn't say p,q real, though you may assume so. If you used an assumption, state it.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: No info about p,q, so cannot fix.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You didn't assume an unstated fact; you held judgment.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You may flip every sign. Check sum and product before deciding.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.o.d: It is a double root, same as 1+i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You treat 'one root known' as 'both roots equal.'
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.info: New information: p,q are real. If other root s+ti (s,t real), sum (1+s)+(1+t)i and product (s−t)+(s+t)i must both be real. Product calculation: (1+i)(s+ti)=s+ti+si+ti².
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.after: For sum real, 1+t=0, t=−1; for product real, s+t=0, s=1. Other root 1−i. Earlier 'cannot determine' was right due to insufficient info; now info changes judgment.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You match imaginary part for real sum but don't check product. Is product real?
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: If roots same, sum 2+2i not real. Check sum reality.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: New info gives two equations (sum and product), but you keep withholding judgment.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This is value of s,t making both sum and product real.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Change info: drop p,q real; instead other root is 2. Then x²+px+q=(x−(1+i))(x−2)=x²−(3+i)x+(2+2i), so p=−3−i,q=2+2i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.after: Here p=−3−i,q=2+2i are non-real, outside 'real coefficients' assumption. Without that assumption, root 1+i alone doesn't guarantee other root 1−i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Without p,q real assumption, cannot say other root 1−i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You distinguish assumption supporting conjugate-root property.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: If one root 1+i, other is always 1−i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Look again at other root in example just made.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Quadratic roots are always one real and one imaginary number.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Roots 1+i and 2 may look like that pair, but root types depend on coefficients. Consider case where both roots are real with real coefficients.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Even with p,q real, other root may not be 1−i.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: p,q in example are not real. Check what conditions were used.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.info: Last info: p,q real again, but one root 1+√2, which isn't imaginary. Example other root 3 gives (x−(1+√2))(x−3)=x²−(4+√2)x+3+3√2; p=−4−√2,q=3+3√2 both real.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.ask: Can you say other root is 1−√2?
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.after: Real p,q alone do not fix other root to 1−√2. That conjugate is guaranteed only with stronger condition p,q rational. Figures: 1 2 1 2.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.o.a: If p,q real, it always is 1−√2.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.r.a: Check other root in example just given.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.o.b: It must be double root, same as 1+√2.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.r.b: You treat 'one root known' as 'double root.'
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.r.c: You carry imaginary-root rule over, only flipping sign. Check sum/product.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.o.d: Cannot fix it. Other root could be 3 while p,q real.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.st.3.r.d: You confirmed by example real coefficients alone aren't enough.
y-m-36-03.s.s1.reflect: At first no info, so 'cannot fix' right. When p,q real info arrived, judgment became 1−i. Next steps used examples to find when rule breaks. Review what information came and when judgment changed or stayed.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.prompt: Choose all cases where other root is necessarily its conjugate (only sign changes).
y-m-36-03.s.s2.hint.0: For every option, choose another root freely and check whether resulting p,q meet condition.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.hint.1: An option with even one counterexample satisfying it is not guaranteed.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.o.a: One root of quadratic with all-real coefficients is 3−2i
y-m-36-03.s.s2.r.a: You checked both needed conditions: imaginary root given and coefficients real.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.o.b: One root of quadratic with complex coefficients is 3−2i
y-m-36-03.s.s2.r.b: Recall earlier counterexample; without real-coefficient assumption, is rule guaranteed?
y-m-36-03.s.s2.o.c: One root of quadratic with rational coefficients is 2+√3
y-m-36-03.s.s2.r.c: This distinguishes coefficient condition needed for real irrational roots too.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.o.d: One root of quadratic with all-real coefficients is 2+√3
y-m-36-03.s.s2.r.d: You treat conditions for imaginary and irrational roots alike. Recall example other root 3.
y-m-36-03.s.s2.explain: With real coefficients, imaginary root comes with conjugate; with rational coefficients, 2+√3 comes with 2−√3. For complex coefficients, or merely real ones, an irrational root doesn't fix its conjugate as the other root.

y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This says no because value small, though 1 positive. Need value greater than 0.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.0.o.d: More tests no tell, so cannot decide.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You no distinguish adding examples from checking expression shape directly.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.info: At x=2 value is 4−8+k=k−4, and this is minimum value. 2
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.ask: Then what range for k expect?
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.after: Minimum k−4 decides. If k>4 all positive; k<4 negative at x=2. Boundary k=4 must test directly.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This expects minimum k−4 must be >0.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This expects minimum k−4≥0. Before boundary test k=4, reasonable guess.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You may treat earlier checked k=5 as boundary. Test k=4.5.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This expects positive k means expression always positive. Try k=1 at x=2.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.info: Boundary k=4: x²−4x+4=(x−2)². At x=2 value 0; elsewhere positive.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.ask: For x²−4x+k>0 all real x, include k=4?
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.after: At x=2 value 0, so >0 fails; exclude k=4, range k>4. If expected b, test changes it; if a, confirms.

y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You read all real numbers as almost all real numbers.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Cannot tell without seeing the problem.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Could test boundary directly, but you did not.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Not included. At x=2 value 0, so >0 fails.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You know failure at one x means not true for all x.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.info: Now change sign: when does x²−4x+k≥0 hold for all real x?
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.after: (x−2)²≥0 for all x, so k=4 included, range k≥4. Boundary depends on > or ≥.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.o.a: Included. At x=2 value 0, and ≥0 allows it.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.r.a: You judge based on whether 0 allowed at boundary.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.o.b: Not included; excluded before for same reason.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.r.b: You ignore inequality sign changed from prior problem.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.o.c: Cannot tell. Must solve quadratic inequality again whenever sign changes.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.st.3.r.c: Could decide by substituting k=4 directly.
y-m-36-05.s.s1.reflect: At first a few values reasonably left uncertainty. Boundary substitution decided inclusion; changing inequality sign changed boundary judgment. Say what changed it and what kept it.
